column12: Judgement on the comparator. Jakafi is the anchor the book's bomedemstat seed uses for the same disease, so the two ET entrants price alike; it is Incyte's own MPN drug and the only branded MPN cytoreductive with a CMS row in the book (Inrebic and Ojjaara are MF-only). Case against, which is strong: Jakafi is not labelled in ET in the US, and ruxolitinib was not superior to best available therapy in hydroxyurea-resistant or intolerant ET (MAJIC-ET, Harrison et al., Blood 2017;130:1889, doi:10.1182/blood-2017-05-785790: complete response 46.6% vs 44.2%). Besremi (ropeginterferon alfa-2b), FDA-approved in ET on 2026-08-31 regardless of genotype or prior therapy (PharmaEssentia release, businesswire.com/news/home/20260831907028/en), is now the closest marketed comparator in the same disease and setting. It launched in PV in 2021 at a WAC of $6,988 a syringe, $153,736 a year at 22 syringes (Anton Rx Report, antonhealth.com/fda-approves-new-tx-for-polycythemia-vera-besremi/; KBR, koreabiomed.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=24488). The ET trials dose 500 ug every 2 weeks from week 4 (SURPASS-ET, Mesa et al., Lancet Haematol 2025;12:e862; EXCEED-ET, Reeves et al., Lancet Reg Health Am 2026;61:101529), 26 syringes, so $181,688 a year at the 2021 WAC, 37% above this figure (the 22-syringe figure is the PV basis, 16% above). Besremi is not used because its current WAC was not found (a Drugs.com cash price near $10,187 a syringe appeared in search, a cash price rather than a WAC, which suggests the 2021 WAC is stale), no discount for it can be sourced (PharmaEssentia gross-to-net searched, not found), it has no CMS row in the book, and a WAC is a full-year list figure while CMS per beneficiary is gross over part-years, so the two are not like for like. The direction of the error is likely down: this anchor probably understates a first mutation-targeted antibody's price. Route: INCA033989 is dosed IV every 2 weeks in Phase 1; Incyte licensed Enable's enFuse on-body delivery system for it (October 2025, 10-Q 0000879169-26-000056) and Halozyme's ENHANZE for a subcutaneous form (July 2026, 8-K 0000879169-26-000053), and started a subcutaneous Phase 1 in patients in Q2 2026. The Phase 3 route was not confirmed. An IV infusion in clinic would be billed under Part B; a self-administered subcutaneous product would sit in Part D with the anchor

Three filters for the Phase 3 entry criteria (CALR-mutated ET, resistant or intolerant to at least one cytoreductive therapy). (1) CALR mutation in 32% of 299 Mayo Clinic ET patients (Tefferi et al., Leukemia 2014;28:2300, doi:10.1038/leu.2014.148, PMID 24791854). (2) 33% of prevalent US ET patients received cytoreductive treatment in 2023 (Veeva Compass claims, ISPOR 2025 poster; the book's bomedemstat eligible_pct, reused). (3) 33 of 166 hydroxyurea-treated ET patients (19.9%) met the ELN criteria for resistance or intolerance over a median 4.5 years (Hernandez-Boluda et al., Br J Haematol 2011;152:81, doi:10.1111/j.1365-2141.2010.08430.x, PMID 21083657). 0.32 x 0.33 x 0.1988 = 0.020993
column12: About 2,662 US patients in the book's pool and 101 a year from incidence. The filters are assumed independent; CALR patients are younger with higher platelet counts, which pulls treatment rates in both directions. Case for higher: SURPASS-ET says 'about a third' of hydroxyurea-treated patients become resistant or intolerant (Mesa et al., Lancet Haematol 2025;12:e862, doi:10.1016/S2352-3026(25)00264-9), a statement rather than a count, and a prevalent treated population has been on therapy longer than 4.5 years; the Phase 3 also admits failure of any cytoreductive, not only hydroxyurea. Case for lower: 28% CALR in the 402-patient Mayo plus Italy cohort (Tefferi et al., Am J Hematol 2014, PMID 24753125); 15% met modified ELN criteria in 148 high-risk Korean ET patients (Park et al., Cancer Med 2023, PMID 36622093). The engine feeds the pool at incidence x eligible_pct, which understates the real inflow of patients newly failing hydroxyurea each year

column12: Stated to show it was considered. Not a line of cancer therapy in the sense of the zero-carryover rule: a CALR-mutated patient who has failed a cytoreductive and is not started this year stays on anagrelide, interferon or continued hydroxyurea and stays eligible for years, given near two-decade survival. The bomedemstat seed on the same pool also carries forward (no value set). Case against: a patient well controlled on a second agent may never switch, which the penetration rate, not the carryover, should carry. Second reader, for the 1.0 against 0: the eligible population is defined by having failed at least one cytoreductive, a status a patient keeps after moving to anagrelide or Besremi, so a patient not started this year is still label-eligible the next, unlike a cancer line where a patient not started moves on and leaves it (forecast.py derive_new_patients docstring). The one leak 1.0 ignores is death: a 19.8-year median survival is about 3.4% a year if exponential (a carryover of 0.966), and resistance with anaemia carried higher mortality (Hernandez-Boluda et al. 2011), so the true figure is a little below 1.0. At 0.966 the engine's US treated stock peaks at 862 rather than 1,012 (15% lower). Kept at 1.0 so the two ET entrants on one pool carry alike (the bomedemstat seed sets none, so 1.0)
